**1B.6 Research Note: Andrés Manuel López Obrador in 2024**

I found **no direct 2024 evidence** that AMLO faced, enabled, or resisted proliferation by allies, proxies, clients, or domestic factions in a concrete way. Mexico is a non-nuclear-weapon state, so the available record is mostly about **institutional nonproliferation discipline** and **support for the Treaty of Tlatelolco / OPANAL**, which is only indirect evidence for this lens.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Mexico promotes peace at the eighth OPANAL course on nuclear disarmament and non-proliferation](https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/mexico-promotes-peace-at-the-eighth-opanal-course-on-nuclear-disarmament-and-non-proliferation?idiom=en) | Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores | 2024-01-26 | https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/mexico-promotes-peace-at-the-eighth-opanal-course-on-nuclear-disarmament-and-non-proliferation?idiom=en | Mexico trained officials from foreign affairs, defense, navy, and security in disarmament and nonproliferation. This supports a reading that the government was building compliance capacity rather than allowing short-term political incentives to weaken nonproliferation discipline. | 1B.6, 1B.4 |
| [Foreign Ministry prioritizes nuclear disarmament on Mexico’s international agenda](https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/foreign-ministry-prioritizes-nuclear-disarmament-on-mexico-s-international-agenda?idiom=en) | Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores | 2024-02-14 | https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/foreign-ministry-prioritizes-nuclear-disarmament-on-mexico-s-international-agenda?idiom=en | Mexico explicitly framed its diplomacy around a safer, more peaceful world grounded in international law and cooperation rather than weapons. This is evidence of anti-proliferation and de-escalatory intent, not tolerance of proliferation for political gain. | 1B.6, 1B.4, 1B.2 |
| [Communiqué of the Member States of OPANAL on the occasion of the 57th Anniversary of the Treaty of Tlatelolco](https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/communique-of-the-member-states-of-opanal-on-the-occasion-of-the-57th-anniversary-of-the-treaty-of-tlatelolco) | Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores | 2024-02-14 | https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/communique-of-the-member-states-of-opanal-on-the-occasion-of-the-57th-anniversary-of-the-treaty-of-tlatelolco | OPANAL members, including Mexico, reaffirmed that nuclear-weapon-free zones are a step toward complete disarmament under effective international control and emphasized verifiable, irreversible, transparent, complete disarmament. This is the clearest 2024 evidence for resistance to proliferation norms and verification-based restraint. | 1B.6, 1B.4 |
| [Mexico chairs OPANAL General Conference](https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/mexico-chairs-opanal-general-conference?idiom=en) | Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores | 2024-11-28 | https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/mexico-chairs-opanal-general-conference?idiom=en | Mexico reiterated commitment to the Treaty of Tlatelolco and to a world free of nuclear weapons, while participants reaffirmed disarmament, non-proliferation, and dialogue with nuclear-weapon states. This indicates sustained good-faith opposition to proliferation, not accommodation of it. | 1B.6, 1B.4 |
| [With World at Delicate Crossroads, Disarmament Committee’s Responsibility ‘Immense’, Says General Assembly President During Robust Debate](https://press.un.org/en/2024/gadis3737.doc.htm) | United Nations, Meetings Coverage and Press Releases | 2024-10-08 | https://press.un.org/en/2024/gadis3737.doc.htm | Mexico’s representative urged fewer warheads, progress on disarmament, and less rhetoric threatening nuclear use, and rejected the idea that nuclear weapons are part of the solution. This supports a general posture of resisting proliferation and reinforcing anti-nuclear norms. | 1B.6, 1B.4, 1B.2 |

**Bottom line**

- Best-supported reading: **yes, AMLO’s government resisted proliferation in the sense of consistently reinforcing nonproliferation and disarmament norms in 2024.**
- This is **indirect** evidence, not a case of resisting a named ally/proxy/client/domestic faction trying to proliferate.
- I found **no reliable counterevidence** showing AMLO tolerated or encouraged proliferation for short-term political advantage.

**Search gap**

- I did not find a 2024 Mexico-specific episode involving allies, proxies, clients, or domestic factions seeking nuclear proliferation.
- Because Mexico has no nuclear weapons program, the evidence base is diplomatic and institutional rather than operational.
